concept.name: Supertrend
concept.definition: An ATR-based trend-following overlay (Olivier Seban, 2009) that plots a single line below price in uptrends and above it in downtrends, at a distance of multiplier x ATR from the bar midpoint, flipping sides when price closes through the line.
concept.intuition: It is a volatility-adjusted trailing stop: wider when the market is volatile, tighter when calm, so ordinary noise does not stop you out but a genuine reversal does.
concept.mechanics: Basic upper band = (H+L)/2 + m x ATR(n), basic lower = (H+L)/2 - m x ATR(n), with common defaults n = 10, m = 3. Final bands are ratcheted - the upper band can only fall and the lower only rise - until a close crosses the active band, which flips the trend state.
concept.formula: Upper = (High + Low)/2 + Multiplier x ATR(n); Lower = (High + Low)/2 - Multiplier x ATR(n); ATR(n) = (ATR_prev x (n-1) + TR)/n (Wilder smoothing).
concept.failure_modes: Lagging by construction and whipsaw-prone in sideways markets; it signals direction only - not trend strength - and results are sensitive to the (period, multiplier) choice.
concept.misconceptions: A green (uptrend) line is not a standalone buy recommendation, and the plotted line is a stop level, not a price target.
concept.example: High 20.23, low 19.04, ATR 1.15, multiplier 1: upper band = 19.635 + 1.15 = 20.79, lower = 18.48 (Investopedia's worked example).
